svg.title: WhistleSim: signal path and physical model
svg.text: WhistleSim: from WARBL's sensors to the sound in the room
A time-domain physical model of a fipple flute (whistle or recorder). Pitch, half-holing, slides and overblowing come from the simulated air column and jet, not from a fingering table.

g.text: MIDI thread: decode, time, queue (lock-free SPSC)
Audio thread, per block (128–512 samples at 44.1/48 kHz)

svg.text: 2 · Inside the model: one sample at ≈ 96 kHz

The jet and the air column form a feedback loop. The sound's flow through the window deflects the jet; the deflection grows on its way to the edge and decides how much of the jet goes into the pipe; that flow drives the sound.
bore: digital waveguide sections ≤ 3 cm (8 mm in a stepped head), a scattering junction at every tone hole
sound's flow through the window, v = Q / A_w,
pushes the jet sideways as it leaves the flue

g.text: The loop, and why harder blowing changes register
breath p → jet speed U → jet leaves the flue, deflected by the window flow v → travels to the edge in τ = W / (0.6 U),
amplified most near f = 0.02 U / h → splits in/out at the edge → jet-drive pressure Δp → pushes the window's air into the
bore → waves reflect from the first open hole and the foot → back at the window as v. The loop sounds where the bore
resonates and the jet's delay and band fit. Blow harder: U rises, τ shortens and the jet's band moves up, so the
first resonance stops fitting and the second (an octave up) takes over. Hysteresis and thresholds come out of this.

svg.text: Numbers match the callouts above. ρ air density, c speed of sound, ν kinematic viscosity, h windway height, W window length, A_w window area.

g.text: The air in the windway (length L) has mass, so the
jet speed U lags the breath: time constant L/U,
≈ 1 ms soft, ≈ 0.3 ms hard. Steady state is
Laminar boundary layers on both walls (Blasius)
carry less flow than the core, down to Poiseuille
Disturbances ride the jet at κU, so the window flow
reaches the edge τ later (fractional delay line).
The jet amplifies most in a band around f_c: 1–2
band-pass stages, retuned as U changes.
η = G exp(0.38 W/h) · h · v_filtered / U
Growth across the window (α_i ≈ 0.38/h). A slower
jet can get extra growth for long waves only; a
steady pressure across it bends it (≤ half-width).
Voicing: Jet Strouhal, Q, convection, stages, gain,
Q_j = H b U · share · tanh((η − y_e) / b)
The part of the jet (half-width b ≈ 0.4h, widening
when turbulent) that goes into the pipe. tanh is the
nonlinearity: square flow when the jet swings far.
y_e: edge offset, plus tilt and bend.
Δp = ρ δ_d / A_w · dQ_j/dt, δ_d = (4/π)√(2hW)
Jet-drive model (Verge, Fabre, Hirschberg): the jet
flow switching sides acts as a pressure source
Losses from vortices shed at the edge: limits the
Window: the source meets the bore
p_top = Δp + Δp_v + noise − M dU_w/dt
The window's air (inertance M = ρ t_w / A_w)
is in series with the bore: open-end-like at low
frequencies, nearly closed at high ones.
p_top = p⁺ + p⁻, U_w = (p⁺ − p⁻) / Z₀
Solved for the outgoing wave p⁺ with the
The window radiates like a hole: its outer mass
in parallel with ρc/A_w takes energy out (∝ f²),
damping high resonances that would ring at the
p(x, t) = p⁺(t − x/c) + p⁻(t + x/c)
Two delay lines per section (≤ 3 cm, ≤ 64 sections),
read with 3rd-order Lagrange fractional delays. Area
changes (stepped heads, tapers) scatter at the
Viscous and thermal wall losses (Keefe) slow the
wave as much as they damp it. One biquad per
Geometry: bore length, radius profile, wall loss
p = Σ · G / (G + Y_hole), G = (S₁ + S₂)/ρc
Every hole is a shunt at a bore junction. Its open
part is a short tube to outside: inner mass + outer
mass ∥ ρc/A (radiation), scaled by the openness.
Its covered part is the chimney's trapped air, a
compliance that flattens notes below it.
A hovering finger at height d: viscous flow out
through the ring under it, and an extra chimney
length b² ln(R/b) / 2d. 3rd order in s, bilinear
Half-holing, shading and slides are physical: no
fingering chart is consulted while playing.
Open end: inverted reflection through a lowpass,
end correction 0.61a. With a bell sensor the foot
Each opening is a monopole: its outgoing flow,
delayed by its extra path to the listener, summed
as two sources: the window, and the holes + foot.
They are placed apart at the ears and in the room.
Then DC blocker, decimation to the host rate,
output gain (1.0 = 2 Pa = 100 dB SPL), and a
restart from rest if it ever goes unstable.
Band noise at the edge: enters the bore like the
tone (coloured by its resonances), partly escapes
directly, and wobbles the jet a little. Pulsed as
the jet sweeps the edge: heard as breathiness.
Attack chiff: a jet that has just started is
turbulent above Re = Uh/ν ≈ 1000–3000, until the
oscillation locks it across the edge.
Finger landing: pushes a flow πb²·v into the
hole's junction and knocks the body (3 damped
Voicing: Breath noise, Direct noise, Pulsing,
Attack chiff, Finger tap, Body knock
Acoustics.cpp: the same geometry in the frequency domain (transfer matrices) gives the window impedance and resonances for the tuning table and Tune holes.
ScalePlan: runs the model offline to find each note's
breath pressure for the test scale. WhistleCheck: CLI.
